reading: Each green box with a one-cell nub gets a mirror copy placed on the side opposite the nub, one cell gap away, with the nub mirrored outward. Copies placed left/right are colour 1; copies placed above/below are colour 8.

slots.subject: each object (box plus nub)
slots.colour: 1 if the copy is horizontal from the source, 8 if vertical

why: every object gets exactly one mirrored copy at distance 1 on the side away from its nub

reading: The grid is split into a few solid colour regions sprinkled with noise dots of one colour. The output is a 1x1 grid of the region colour that holds the most noise dots.

slots.output: 1x1 of the region colour containing the most noise cells

why: the output colour's region contains strictly more noise cells than any other region

reading: Scattered single dots are removed and packed into the rectangle outlines as a checkerboard (interior top-left cell filled). Each outline gets the dot colour whose dot count equals the checkerboard cell count of its interior.

slots.dots: isolated scatter cells, grouped by colour
slots.match: colour whose dot count = ceil(interior area / 2)

why: per colour, dots removed = checker cells added; colour counts are preserved

reading: Starting from the 1 at the bottom-left, a diagonal line of 1 goes up-right and bounces off the left/right walls in a zigzag to the top; every other cell becomes 8.

slots.path: diagonal up, reflecting at side borders

why: exactly one 1 per row, column changes by one per row and reverses at the borders

reading: The top-left 3x3 window (fenced by a 5 row and column) is a template; its exact copy appears once elsewhere in the noise grid, and a 5x5 ring of colour 5 is drawn around that copy.

slots.match: the other position where the 3x3 window is identical
slots.mark: ring of 5 on the 5x5 box around the match

why: only cells on the ring around the unique exact template match change, all to 5
invariants: template corner and all other cells unchanged

reading: The grid is made of full-width or full-height colour stripes with noise pixels; every stripe is repainted entirely in its majority colour.

slots.stripes: maximal runs of rows (or columns) sharing a majority colour

why: each output stripe is uniform and equals the input stripe's most common colour
invariants: stripe boundaries and grid size unchanged

reading: A grey column splits the grid in half; the right half is folded onto the left half (mirrored about the grey column) and overlaid, and the left half is output.
why: output cell = left cell if non-zero else the mirrored right cell; no colour conflicts occur
invariants: output width = width of left panel

reading: Above a 6 landscape in a 1 field, the 1 cells in the column where the 1s reach deepest become 9, and the 1 cells in the column where the 6s rise highest become 4 (rightmost on ties).

slots.column B: column whose 6 top is highest (rightmost if tied)
slots.colours: 9 on column A's 1 cells, 4 on column B's 1 cells

why: only 1 cells in exactly two columns change

reading: The small red (2) shape is copied into some of the places in the grey/black noise where it fits entirely on 0 cells, without overlapping other copies.

slots.anchors: positions where the unit fits on 0 cells (non-overlapping; selection rule unclear)

why: every new 2 cell was 0 and belongs to a translated exact copy of the shape

reading: Each green rectangle spawns two diagonal cascades of copies going down-left and down-right, each step offset by its own height down and its own width sideways, until leaving the grid (clipped at the border).
why: all new cells are translated copies of a rectangle along its two downward diagonals
